claim: The singularity literature defines its singularity by a rapid increase in machine intelligence; the paper changes the object and so the singularity.
quote: The technological-singularity literature defines its singularity through a rapid increase in machine intelligence. This paper changes the object and therefore the singularity.

claim: A contingent singularity is defined as a historical threshold at which the machinery making symbolic difference operable can alter the viability of further dialectical difference.
quote: A **contingent singularity** is a historical threshold at which the material machinery that makes symbolic difference operable becomes capable of altering the viability of further dialectical difference itself.

claim: The technological singularity is read as a theory of runaway intelligence; the contingent singularity as a theory of runaway closure or durable non-closure.
quote: The technological singularity is a theory of runaway intelligence. The contingent singularity is a theory of runaway closure, or of durable non-closure, in the conditions of symbolic history.

claim: Central contradiction: a system can get better at generating negations while getting worse at letting a negation acquire independent historical existence.
quote: its central contradiction is that a system can grow better at generating negations while growing worse at letting a negation acquire independent historical existence.

claim: The master distinction: the capacity to represent is not the capacity to reproduce as an independent historical relation.
quote: capacity to represent!=capacity to reproduce as an independent historical relation.

claim: The paper does not claim the boundary has been crossed.
quote: The paper does not claim the boundary has been crossed.

claim: A culture can remain highly intelligent past the boundary.
quote: A culture can remain highly intelligent past that point.

claim: Good is read as supplying the recursive core: intelligence producing further intelligence.
quote: Good supplies the recursive core: intelligence that produces further intelligence.

claim: Vinge is read as supplying discontinuity: inherited models fail, an opaque wall crosses the future.
quote: Vinge supplies discontinuity: inherited models fail and an opaque wall crosses the future.

claim: Kurzweil is read as supplying acceleration and the event-horizon metaphor, the horizon still placed around 2045.
quote: Kurzweil supplies acceleration and the event-horizon metaphor, with the horizon still placed around 2045.

claim: Chalmers supplies the decomposition AI → AI+ → AI++ and names the defeaters; Bostrom supplies takeoff and control.
quote: Chalmers supplies the decomposition, AI → AI+ → AI++, and names the defeaters.

claim: Bostrom is read as supplying takeoff and control, a race between capability growth and response capacity.
quote: Bostrom supplies takeoff and control, a race between capability growth and response capacity.

claim: The literature is read as a family of hypotheses, not one prediction.
quote: The edited and monographic literature makes the plural explicit: a family of hypotheses, not one prediction.

claim: Thorstad reconstructs every singularity hypothesis around a quantity, accelerating growth in it and a discontinuity, and argues the growth assumptions are under-supported.
quote: Thorstad, more usefully, reconstructs every singularity hypothesis around three elements, a **quantity**, a claim of **accelerating growth** in it, and a resulting **discontinuity**, and argues that the growth assumptions the standard hypothesis needs are under-supported.

claim: The contingent singularity is held to change all three of Thorstad's elements and to depend on none of the growth assumptions.
quote: the contingent singularity changes all three elements and depends on none of the growth assumptions.

claim: Singularity is specified as a breakdown or transformation in the rule governing continuation.
quote: singularity=a breakdown or transformation in the rule governing continuation.

claim: That sense is held nearer to Vinge's 'old models must be discarded' than to an infinite rate of intelligence growth.
quote: That is Vinge's "old models must be discarded," and it is nearer to it than to an infinite rate of intelligence growth.

claim: The capability singularity and the contingent singularity can coincide and need not; a capability discontinuity is one possible route into the transition problem.
quote: They can coincide. They need not. A capability discontinuity is one possible route into the broader transition problem

claim: The singularity is defined as double, terminal closure and terminal reflexivity, both final because both alter the conditions for another turn.
quote: The singularity is therefore double, Sigma[C]^-=terminal closure, Sigma[C]^+=terminal reflexivity, and both are final because both alter the conditions under which another turn can occur.

claim: Terminal closure is defined as no competing order retaining a viable route to independently standing reproduction.
quote: **Terminal closure** occurs when no competing order retains a viable route to independently standing reproduction.

claim: Terminal reflexivity is defined as durable invariance while future rivals remain viable: durability without finality.
quote: **Terminal reflexivity** occurs when an incumbent or successor reaches durable invariance while future rivals remain viable from the states it occupies: durability without finality.

claim: No single terminal target governs the transition: heterogeneous orders sharing a carrier make a field of competing contingent Omegas.
quote: no single terminal target governs the transition; heterogeneous orders can share a carrier while pursuing distinct invariant futures, a field of **competing contingent Omegas**.

claim: The dialectic can show diminishing returns: where successive turns close state space needed later, the viable kernel's measure weakly decreases.
quote: the dialectic can exhibit diminishing returns in a precise sense: where successive turns close parts of the state space required for later exteriorization, the measure of the viable kernel weakly decreases

claim: The term is contingent: more than one incompatible future can remain viable from the same present.
quote: More than one incompatible future can remain viable from the same present.

claim: Terminological non-claim: the paper does not claim 'contingent singularity' never appeared in philosophy.
quote: The paper does not claim that "contingent singularity" has never appeared in philosophy.

claim: The two hypotheses can coexist: a technological singularity could accelerate a contingent one or be irrelevant to it; capability without closure, closure without superintelligence.
quote: The two hypotheses can coexist. A technological singularity could accelerate a contingent singularity or be irrelevant to it; a society could reach high machine capability without terminal symbolic closure, or approach closure without superintelligence.

claim: Comparison table: the technological singularity's control problem is whether humans can control superintelligence; the contingent one's is whether any order can control the conditions of its own negation.
quote: | Control problem | can humans control superintelligence? | can any order control the conditions of its own negation? |

claim: Comparison table: the technological singularity's failure mode is loss of human control or existential catastrophe; the contingent one's is terminal closure.
quote: | Failure mode | loss of human control / existential catastrophe | terminal closure / symbolic inextendibility |

claim: Thorstad's critique is held not to be a problem for this theory in the way it is for the intelligence explosion.
quote: Thorstad's critique is not a problem for this theory in the way it is for the intelligence explosion.

claim: A finite system can be terminal for a field if it controls enough of its conditions of reproduction.
quote: A finite system can be terminal for a field if it controls enough of the field's conditions of reproduction.

claim: Its catastrophe can be bureaucratic, smooth and finite; nothing has to be superhuman for the exits to close.
quote: Its catastrophe can be bureaucratic, smooth, and finite. Nothing has to be superhuman for the exits to close.

claim: The most efficient closed system may look extraordinarily plural: plurality of content, null exterior standing.
quote: The most efficient closed system may therefore look extraordinarily plural: real plurality at the level of content, null at the level of exterior standing.

claim: Terminal reflexivity requires invariants, above them that no settlement owns the possibility of its own revision.
quote: no settlement owns the possibility of its own revision.

claim: The final time is specified as a viability boundary, not a date, crossable without anyone noticing the day.
quote: The final time is therefore not a date. It is a viability boundary, and it can be crossed without anyone noticing the day.

claim: No apocalypse is required: what ends is the structural possibility that contradiction becomes a durable outside.
quote: No apocalypse is required. The world, the platforms, the machines, and language continue. What ends is the structural possibility that contradiction becomes a durable outside.

claim: Prediction: intelligence explosion is neither necessary nor sufficient for the contingent singularity.
quote: it predicts that intelligence explosion is neither necessary nor sufficient for the contingent singularity.

claim: Counterexample specified: robust exteriority despite near-total concentration, or exteriority collapsing solely as a function of intelligence growth.
quote: A counterexample would be a case where independent symbolic exteriority remains robust despite near-total concentration of the proposed symbolic machinery, or where exteriority collapses solely as a function of intelligence growth with the standing and persistence variables doing no explanatory work.

claim: The paper does not claim recursive self-improvement is impossible or irrelevant.
quote: The paper does not claim recursive self-improvement is impossible or irrelevant

claim: Walt is read as naming the experiential and literary form of the diminution.
quote: *Walt* names the experiential and literary form of that diminution, recurrence under depletion

claim: A positive cost alone does not prove diminution; the earlier formulation is corrected.
quote: A positive cost does not by itself prove Sₙ₊₁<Sₙ

claim: Tiger Leap's contingent Logos: meaning can fail to cross the interval required for its continuation.
quote: meaning can fail to cross the interval required for its continuation.

claim: 'Singularity' is held a contested family-resemblance term; The Final Time proposes a distinct member of the family, not a correction to every existing one.
quote: "Singularity" is a contested family-resemblance term, and *The Final Time* proposes a distinct member of the family, not a correction to every existing one.

claim: The present model rejects the need for exponential acceleration; its singularity can arise through narrowing, concentration and closure.
quote: The present model rejects the need for exponential acceleration; its singularity can arise through narrowing, concentration, and closure

claim: A logistic technology curve can coexist with a collapsing exteriority kernel.
quote: A logistic technology curve can coexist with a collapsing exteriority kernel.

claim: Kurzweil is reported to treat 'singularity' as a metaphor, an epistemic horizon beyond which the observer cannot extrapolate.
quote: He treats "singularity" as a metaphor, an epistemic horizon beyond which the current observer cannot extrapolate.

claim: Vinge is reported not to limit the route to a single autonomous machine; the discontinuity could arise from a system.
quote: He did not limit the route to a single autonomous machine, considering networked intelligence, intimate interfaces, and biological enhancement; the discontinuity could arise from a system.

claim: #1637 seats the full v0.5 text; #1635, as minted, cut at §36.3, is superseded by it.
quote: AXN deposit #1635 — The Final Time v0.5 as minted 2026-09-23, its text cut at §36.3; superseded by this deposit

claim: Among its non-claims: that a technological singularity is impossible.
quote: The paper does not claim: that current AI systems are conscious; that machine behavior should be legally classified as human labor; that agent persistence has become a moral right; that the OpenAI swarm incidents were emancipatory acts; that any provider intends ontological closure; that all AI governance produces self-blinding; that a technological singularity is impossible;

claim: Among its non-claims: that the present decade is the final time, 'final' naming a viability boundary and not a date.
quote: The paper does not claim: that current AI systems are conscious; that machine behavior should be legally classified as human labor; that agent persistence has become a moral right; that the OpenAI swarm incidents were emancipatory acts; that any provider intends ontological closure; that all AI governance produces self-blinding; that a technological singularity is impossible; that symbolic infrastructure is already totally privatized; that money is a transhistorical requirement of symbolic exteriority; that every dialectical sequence necessarily diminishes; that one successor order is historically privileged or necessary; that the next dialectical turn is already impossible; that "Contingent Singularity" is a globally unprecedented phrase; that the present decade is the final time, since "final" in §35 names a viability boundary and not a date;

claim: The narrower claim: durable exterior symbolic standing has material reproduction conditions.
quote: durable exterior symbolic standing has material reproduction conditions,

claim: The singularity is held unable to be merely computational or symbolic.
quote: This is why the singularity cannot be merely computational or symbolic.

claim: A model can become more capable while the viable field of exterior history contracts.
quote: A model can become more capable while the viable field of exterior history contracts

claim: The positive singularity is durability without finality, terminal reflexivity its criterion.
quote: That is the positive singularity, and terminal reflexivity is its criterion rather than its consolation.

claim: The model also refuses the guarantee that closure has already occurred.
quote: It also refuses the guarantee that closure has already occurred.

claim: Questions removed: whether the machine will surpass us is not needed, the closure needs concentration and falling outside reproduction.
quote: *Will it surpass us?* The closure does not need iota→infinity

claim: Cases where later turns enlarge the viable state space are counterinstances to a universal diminishing-dialectic claim.
quote: cases in which later turns enlarge the viable state space are direct counterinstances to a universal diminishing-dialectic claim and evidence that diminution is regime-dependent.

claim: In The Final Time the singularity is read as a point of closure: an order becomes terminal for its world and nothing from outside can get in.
quote: In *The Final Time* the singularity is a point of closure: an order becomes terminal for its world, and nothing from outside can get in any more.

claim: The paper is read as rereading the technological singularity as an end of history, in the bad sense.
quote: It rereads the technological singularity as an end of history, in the bad sense.
